verdict: PG&E's revenue slipped 1% to $6.2 billion and GAAP profit fell, as a lower allowed return on equity and higher Wildfire Fund costs outweighed savings from running the grid more cheaply.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Down from $0.37 a year ago; non-GAAP core EPS was $0.41

kpis.label: Income for common shareholders
kpis.note: Net income was $776M before $27M of preferred dividends

segments.name: Electric
segments.note: Selling electricity to 16 million Californians at regulator-set prices — down 2% YoY.

segments.name: Natural gas
segments.note: Delivering natural gas for heating and cooking — up 2% YoY in this seasonally quiet quarter.

opex.name: Operating & maintenance
opex.note: Running, repairing and making the grid safer day to day — down from $2,641M a year ago as PG&E cuts costs.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of poles, wires and pipes over their long lives — a non-cash charge that grows as PG&E invests.

opex.name: Wildfire Fund expense
opex.note: PG&E's contribution to California's wildfire insurance fund, which covers future wildfire claims.

opex.name: SB 901 securitization charge
opex.note: A charge tied to bonds issued for past wildfire costs under a California law (SB 901).

otherDetail: A net $568M drag: $825M of interest expense, partly offset by $104M of interest income and $153M of other income.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: the cost of electricity bought and generated ($904M) plus the cost of natural gas bought for customers ($109M) are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining lines mirror PG&E's income statement. Net income in the flow is the reported $776M, before $27M of preferred dividends that leave $749M for common shareholders. PG&E recorded an income tax benefit this quarter, so tax adds to profit.
oneTimers: Non-core items totaled $156M after tax ($0.07 per share) — mainly $102M of Wildfire Fund contribution amortization and $42M of strategic repositioning costs, partly offset by a $29M bankruptcy and legal benefit. Excluding them, core earnings were $928M ($0.41 per share).

takeaways.title: A lower allowed return bit
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS fell to $0.34 from $0.37, mainly because regulators lowered PG&E's return on equity for 2026 and last year's tax-method catch-up did not repeat.

takeaways.title: Cost cuts are on track
takeaways.text: Operating and maintenance spending fell to $2,543M from $2,641M — PG&E says it is on track for its 2–4% non-fuel cost reduction target for 2026.

takeaways.title: Burying lines to cut fire risk
takeaways.text: PG&E filed a plan to bury 5,000 miles of power lines, which it says cuts wildfire risk on those lines by 98% — the long-term project behind much of its spending.
